title: Per-head spike detector and iterative layer-rescale generator for hybrid FP8/INT8
creator: Luis Romero
description:
Summary: Production staging runs revealed intermittent quality regressions after applying hybrid FP8/INT8 profiles to several open models. This ticket implements a per-head spike detector (frequency-aware) plus an iterative layer-rescale generator that outputs per-layer multipliers and head-level clip thresholds suitable for FP8 and INT8 calibration.

Goals:
- Detect heads and layers that produce infrequent but high-magnitude spikes and quantify spike frequency across representative prompts.
- Generate per-layer rescale factors that reduce tail mass while retaining median activation fidelity.
- Validate generated profiles using a lightweight simulation harness and a standardized accuracy battery.

Acceptance criteria:
- Generated profiles produce <=2% perplexity regression vs fp32 for 90% of eval prompts across LLama-3-13B, Mistral-large, Qwen-7B.
- Any profile that increases compute by >3% or latency by >5% must be flagged and rejected automatically.
- Profiles must include a deterministic rollback key and be stored with provenance metadata.

Implementation notes:
- Spike detector: run on probe set (~1k prompts) segmented into prompt types; compute per-head percentiles at 99.9 and 99.995 and record spike_rate = fraction of prompts with activations above 99.995. Tag heads with spike_rate > 0.2% as "episodic".
- Rescale generator: for each tagged layer compute multiplier m = max(0.5, min(4.0, median_target / median_observed * damping_factor)). Damping schedules applied across iterations to avoid oscillating multipliers.
- Quant simulation: batch-forward the eval battery under weight/activation quantization (FP8-e4m3 and INT8 per-channel) with noise injection matching measured rounding behavior. Track perplexity, token-accuracies, and a small set of downstream NLG checks (style retention, instruction-follow fidelity).

Progress:
- 2025-02-23 (Luis Romero): Probe harness extension completed and merged to feature branch. Probe outputs include spike_rate CSVs uploaded to s3://redwood-qa/quant-spike-probes/2025-02-23/.
- 2025-02-26 (Aisha Khan): Initial rescale generator prototype implemented. On Qwen-7B the prototype reduced extreme head spikes in attention layers 12-16; simulated perplexity delta improved from 3.7% to 1.2%.
- 2025-03-01 (QA - Ben O'Neill): Ran regression battery: discovered a small cluster of prompts (n=7) where candidate profiles increase repetition rate. Created reproducer and added to examples repo.

Open decisions and mitigations:
- Spike frequency threshold: default 0.2% but tunable per-model. Lower thresholds increase false-positive tuning; higher thresholds allow more regressions.
- Per-model vs per-deployment: prefer model-bundled profiles stored with the model artifact, with runtime override for emergency rollback.

Next steps:
- Harden automated rejection rules and add integration tests for the quant-sim harness (owner: Aisha; due 2025-03-10).
- Run GPU-level validation across staging fleet for LLama-3-13B and Mistral-large (owner: Luis; 2025-03-12 to 2025-03-18).
- Create console panel summarizing spike_rate trends and applied rescale factors (owner: UX team).

References: Confluence doc: HetOutlier calibration plan; internal repos: calib-harness, runtime-quant; staging dashboards and S3 probes.
